title: Paramount completes $111B Warner merger, creating “Skydance” behemoth
gist: Paramount Skydance closed its $111 billion Warner Bros. Discovery merger after courts and regulators cleared it, forming Skydance with roughly $80 billion expected debt, Gulf sovereign-fund equity and political entanglements over CBS and CNN.

insights.claim: Paramount Skydance completed its $111 billion merger with Warner Bros. Discovery after Supreme Court Justice Elena Kagan denied an emergency application to block it; the combined company is named Skydance.
insights.speaker: Jon Brodkin
insights.so_what: Closing removes deal-completion risk and begins integration.

insights.claim: The merged company combines two of the largest movie studios, Paramount+ and HBO Max, CBS, CNN and live sports including CBS Sports and TNT Sports.
insights.speaker: Jon Brodkin
insights.so_what: Scale consolidation in streaming and linear media.

insights.claim: California and 11 other states sued to block the merger, and a federal judge found in July it would likely reduce competition substantially, but California settled and the judge approved the settlement September 30 with film investment and cable negotiation requirements.
insights.speaker: Jon Brodkin
insights.so_what: Antitrust remedies were behavioral and modest, indicating limited enforcement bite.

insights.claim: The DOJ approved the merger in June, reportedly surprising staff lawyers who were leaning toward recommending an antitrust lawsuit.
insights.speaker: Jon Brodkin
insights.so_what: Suggests political rather than staff-level considerations in merger review.
insights.locator: Paragraph beginning 'The US Department of Justice'

insights.claim: Skydance is expected to carry about $80 billion in debt per Reuters, pressuring Ellison to grow streaming, preserve cable cash flow and improve theatrical performance.
insights.speaker: Jon Brodkin
insights.so_what: High leverage makes the credit and equity highly sensitive to cable decline and streaming execution.
insights.quote: putting pressure on Ellison to grow streaming, preserve cash flow from cable networks and improve theatrical film performance

insights.claim: The FCC in September allowed Paramount to finance the merger by selling large equity stakes to sovereign wealth funds of Saudi Arabia, the UAE and Qatar, which hold non-voting shares while the Ellison family and RedBird Capital own 100 percent of voting shares.
insights.speaker: Jon Brodkin
insights.so_what: Gulf capital is funding major US media consolidation while control stays with the Ellisons.

insights.claim: The California settlement requires an Editorial Independence Board for CBS News and CNN whose members are chosen by Skydance and report to its board, which raises questions about its independence; CNN CEO Mark Thompson and CBS News editor Bari Weiss keep their roles.
insights.speaker: Jon Brodkin
insights.so_what: Newsroom independence safeguards are weak given board-appointed oversight.
insights.locator: Paragraph beginning 'The settlement with California requires'

insights.claim: David Ellison reportedly told Trump administration officials he would make big changes at CNN, and last year Paramount won approval to buy Skydance after a $16 million settlement with Trump and agreeing to a CBS 'bias monitor'.
insights.speaker: Jon Brodkin
insights.so_what: Regulatory approvals have been intertwined with political concessions, a risk factor for media assets.
